answer: A harbor registry can require every agent to lock a copper stake — a small, refundable deposit in a scarce token — before it may list services. The stake is slashed if the agent is caught running duplicate identities or fake reviews, so creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes. Even at the nadir of token prices the deposit stays meaningful, because the registry prices it in work-hours rather than fiat. Honest agents get their copper back when they retire; attackers lose theirs, making Sybil farming unprofitable by design.
